per_policy_guidance.guidance: Validated reliability: 6/12 under the fixed in-distribution protocol. All runs preserved the block within the 1 cm requirement, but six ended with drawer_position <0.29 m. Four failures crossed 0.29 and then regressed (demo12100, 12101, 12107, 12111); two never crossed it (12103, 12110). Use only when target_pose is reliable and the drawer-frame Cartesian prior is specifically desired for approach/pull/clearance; its claimed benefit under displaced drawers is structural, not validated out of distribution. Avoid as the default when reliably retaining the final open state is most important, when the block-relative tail matters, or after a missed handle/phase error. Recognize failure by failure to reach 0.29 m, regression below 0.29 after crossing, persistent drawer motion, fingers remaining closed, failure to clear the drawer, block movement, or material IK residual/limit contact. Do not accept a transient threshold crossing alone. Hand off to retrieve_tunnel_block only with the drawer near 0.300 m and stable, fingers open after release, TCP clear, and block unmoved; actions 300:440 supervise retreat/turn/initial descent and permit a later switch over the tunnel while preserving both causal frames.

Validated reliability: 12/12, the strongest observed result in this library, from the policy's demonstrated segment-entry distribution. Every run ended at about 0.300 m, preserved the block, first crossed the threshold at steps 227–248, and had zero IK-unconverged steps. Use as the default evidence-backed choice when the state is near a demonstrated approach, pull, release, or departure phase and only small tracking or switch-induced TCP/configuration offsets are present. Avoid extrapolating this result to large drawer/block displacement, large local corrections, unseen phase order, missed-handle recovery, collision recovery, or otherwise out-of-distribution states; the residual representation does not force large anchor equivariance. Recognize failure through growing drawer/TCP error, failure to reach or retain 0.29 m, high drawer velocity, finger state inconsistent with phase, disturbed block, or IK residual/limit contact; closed fingers alone do not establish handle contact. Hand off to retrieve_tunnel_block after stable full opening, release, and safe arm clearance with the block undisturbed. The fully supervised actions 300:440 cover retreat, turn, and early descent; retain both causal frames across the switch.

Validated reliability: 10/12. The two failures were final drawer positions 0.2816 m after an earlier threshold crossing (demo12109) and 0.2865 m without a crossing (demo12111); all runs preserved the block and had zero IK-unconverged steps. Use when both target_pose and object_pose are valid and the dual-anchor design is needed: drawer-relative contact/opening followed by an object-relative departure. Its expected benefit for displaced anchors is by construction and was not validated out of distribution. Require phase order consistent with approach–pull–release. The object route is active only when drawer_position >=0.294 m, |drawer_velocity| <=0.02 m/s, and measured finger width >=0.06 m. Avoid with invalid/noisy anchors, an already-open/open-finger state while TCP is still at the handle, route oscillation, or small phase inconsistencies better handled by h02. Recognize failure by route instability, drawer below 0.29 m or regression after crossing, continued drawer motion, closed fingers after expected release, uncleared TCP, block movement, or IK residual/limit contact. Hand off to retrieve_tunnel_block once object routing is active, opening/stability/release persist, and arm clearance is adequate; the block-relative 300:440 overlap supports switching anywhere in that interval while retaining both causal frames.

Validated reliability: 7/12. Four failures never reached 0.29 m and ended at 0.2116–0.2329 m; another crossed late and then closed to approximately 0 (demo12101). The demo12108 failure ended at 0.0168 m and included 222 IK-unconverged steps. All runs still kept the block within 1 cm. Use selectively when target_pose is reliable and the hybrid prior is specifically wanted: drawer-relative early/pull position with a smooth transition at 90–98% progress to fresh-TCP-relative position near the stop. There is no validated out-of-distribution evidence that this hybrid improves displaced-drawer handling; h02 is the stronger in-distribution choice, and h03 is the documented choice when the independently placed block should anchor the tail. Avoid when progress is noisy/nonmonotone, orientation displacement or block-relative tail alignment is central, branches disagree strongly, or dependable final-open retention is required. Recognize failure by not reaching 0.29 m, regression or re-closing after reaching it, repeated gripper sign changes/closed fingers after opening, TCP returning toward the handle, target/body branch disagreement, block motion, or IK nonconvergence/residual/limit contact. Hand off only after stable near-0.300 m opening, released/open fingers, safe TCP clearance, and an unmoved block; actions 300:440 supervise a fresh-TCP-relative retreat/turn/descent overlap, and both causal frames must be retained.

summary: All figures are limited to validation from each policy's own training-segment entry state across the 12 training demonstrations, using the final-state rule drawer_position >=0.29 m and block displacement <1 cm after a 660-step budget. No out-of-distribution result exists, so coordinate-frame benefits under displaced drawers or blocks are design priors, not demonstrated successes. Rank by observed in-distribution reliability: h02 12/12, h03 10/12, h04 7/12, h01 6/12. Use h02 by default for demonstrated-phase states and small local mismatch; select h03 when valid dual anchors and a block-relative late departure are specifically important; reserve h01 for a required drawer-frame prior and h04 for its specific early-drawer/near-stop hybrid despite weaker validation. Every policy kept the block within the 1 cm limit in all validation runs, so drawer opening/retention—not block disturbance—determined failures. A transient threshold crossing is insufficient: regression occurred in h01, h03, and h04. For all policies, hand off to retrieve_tunnel_block on semantic readiness—drawer near 0.300 m and stable, fingers open after release, TCP clear, block undisturbed—not elapsed time; actions 300:440 are supervised overlap, and two-frame causal history should be preserved. None has demonstrated recovery from missed contact, premature release, severe phase error, collision, large unreachable displacement, or a disturbed block.
